@thesimplekid can you take a look at this? It adds per-call `newly_added_unspent`/`newly_added_pending` to `Restored`, with tests.

I found it a little confusing to compare the three options as stacked commits, so I split them into separate PRs on my fork. Each includes the shared tests and one complete implementation against the same base:

- [Option A: dedicated thread per connection](https://github.com/thesimplekid/cdk/pull/24)
- [Option B: blocking task per operation](https://github.com/thesimplekid/cdk/pull/22)
- [Option C: typed requests to an async actor](https://github.com/thesimplekid/cdk/pull/23)

These are just for comparing the approaches independently. We can keep the design discussion here and use those diffs to review each option.
This PR was closed because it has been inactive for 21 days since being marked as stale.

Could we fix this in the BOLT11 completion logic instead of capping the recorded payment? For a 64-sat quote paid with 65 sats, we could preserve `amount_paid = 65` and consider the quote `ISSUED` once `amount_issued` reaches the quoted 64 sats.

That would also handle existing overpaid quotes without rewriting their payment records. We’d need to align the BOLT11 mintable-amount calculation and test that no further issuance is allowed after completion.

@thesimplekid thanks, good catch. Narrowed it in 97d3ed47: a stored `Pending` proof with no `used_by_operation` is now moved to `Unspent` when the mint reports it unspent. Only the state is updated (`update_proofs_state`), so its derivation index and other metadata stay as they are. `Reserved`, `PendingSpent` and operation-owned `Pending` proofs are still left to their operations, and the scan totals are unchanged.

5ba8ff9d adds `test_restore_releases_unowned_pending_proofs` (two restores: the mint first reports the proof pending, then releases it; on the previous head the proof stayed `Pending`) and `test_restore_keeps_operation_owned_pending_proofs`.
@thesimplekid thanks, done: squashed into a single commit (7a98f4e9). The code is unchanged from the reviewed version.

@thesimplekid thanks for tracing that through. I went with rejecting: in a381ba1e, before saving and overwriting the rows, receive now refuses with `TokenPending` when a stored row is `Pending` for an operation that still has a saga. An unresolved receive therefore keeps its proofs and its snapshot until recovery resolves it, and the retry can be made once it has.

06ae235f adds `test_receive_retry_keeps_proofs_the_wallet_already_stored`: the first receive fails ambiguously, the retry is refused with `TokenPending` without touching the proofs, and recovery then compensates the first receive and restores the original `PendingSpent` row with its send operation.

@thesimplekid agreed, that's cleaner. Reworked in 529c3021: the payment cap is gone and `amount_paid` keeps recording the full 65 sats. A BOLT11 quote can now issue at most its quoted amount, so `amount_mintable` and the quote state use the smaller of `amount_paid` and the quote amount. The quote is `ISSUED` once 64 sats are issued, and quotes that were already overpaid complete the same way without touching their payment records.

1d166993 covers the state/mintable cases (overpaid, overpaid and issued, partly paid) and checks that a second mint request after completion is rejected with `IssuedQuote`. I've also updated the title to match the new approach.

I looked into what xpay guarantees when it returns an error, to answer my own first question. Here is what CLN's source shows, and a rule that lets cdk-cln settle these quotes without giving up fail-closed. A PR implementing it will follow.

**What xpay does** ([`plugins/xpay/xpay.c` @ 8a0a56a](https://github.com/ElementsProject/lightning/blob/8a0a56a25123/plugins/xpay/xpay.c))

- The 209 in this report is "Failed after N attempts … Then routing failed" ([L1925](https://github.com/ElementsProject/lightning/blob/8a0a56a25123/plugins/xpay/xpay.c#L1925)): getroutes found no route for the amount still to be sent.
- Unless `xpay-slow-mode` is set, `should_finish_command` ([L457](https://github.com/ElementsProject/lightning/blob/8a0a56a25123/plugins/xpay/xpay.c#L457)) lets `payment_give_up` return that error at once, even with other parts still in flight. So 209 alone does not prove the payment cannot settle, and you are right to keep it `Unknown`.
- Once xpay has given up, it sends nothing new. A part that fails afterwards hits `/* If xpay is done, return now */` ([L1312](https://github.com/ElementsProject/lightning/blob/8a0a56a25123/plugins/xpay/xpay.c#L1312)) and no further route is requested. The parts already in flight resolve, and that is all.

**The rule this allows**

When an xpay invocation has returned, its outcome is fixed once its in-flight parts resolve. For a payment hash, then:

- if every xpay invocation the mint made for that hash has returned, and
- `listsendpays` shows no `pending` part and no `complete` part for the hash,

no part can still settle, and the quote can be `Failed`. A `complete` part means `Paid`, as now.

This also answers the concern in `xpay_error_state` that `listpays` aggregates by hash. `check_outgoing_unpaided` allows a new dispatch when the state is `Unknown` or `Failed`, so several invocations per hash are possible. The rule therefore has to cover all of them, not only the one that just returned.

**What cdk-cln would need**

- Record each dispatch per payment hash in the existing KV store, the way BOLT12 bindings are kept: open before the `xpay` call, returned after it, whatever the result.
- In `check_outgoing_payment`, map a negative `listpays` status to `Failed` only when no open dispatch remains and `listsendpays` has no pending or complete part. Otherwise keep today's `Unknown`.
- A mint that crashes mid-call leaves its dispatch open, so that quote stays `Unknown`, exactly as today.

Startup recovery and status polls would then settle the quote in this report on their own after the last HTLC fails. The proofs would be released without any operator action.

One gap it cannot close: an xpay started outside the mint, for example an operator paying the same invoice by hand with `lightning-cli`, is invisible to the dispatch record. If that invocation is between attempts at the moment the mint checks, the mint could mark the quote `Failed` while the payment can still go through.

#2762 partially addresses this: it moves SQLite operations onto blocking workers, so a writer waiting for a lock no longer blocks the Tokio worker needed by the transaction holding that lock. It also adds file-backed concurrent-writer regression coverage.

The 10-second busy timeout, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`, and multi-connection pool remain. The PR does not add busy-error retries or a single-writer queue, or change the melt saga's recovery after a transaction fails following payment dispatch. A lock held beyond the timeout can still cause that failure.

The exact probe in this issue would still time out: it keeps transaction A open while awaiting transaction B, without releasing A. Moving B's wait off the async worker does not release A's lock.

I'd keep this issue open for the remaining mid-flow failure/recovery concern, while considering executor starvation under SQLite contention addressed by #2762. Its new tests cover database-level contention, rather than a full mint flow recovering from a post-payment busy timeout.

This assessment is based on inspection of the PR's code and tests; I haven't rerun the probe.

Confirming this in production: an independent checker ([NutCheck](https://nutcheck.org)) finds that all four public CDK mints it tests (testnut, Macadamia, Minibits, WesternBTC on cdk-mintd 0.17.6–0.18.3) accept a P2PK spend whose secret has two `locktime` tags, which NUT-11 says must be rejected. Nutshell fixed the same thing in 0.21.0 (cashubtc/nutshell#1008).

Evidence (proofs redacted): https://nutcheck.org/mints/testnut.cashu.space.html
Reproduce: `uvx --from git+https://github.com/rademenezbtc/nutcheck nutcheck https://testnut.cashu.space` (check `p2pk.malformed`).

The scorecard will show mints passing as they upgrade to a release with this fix.
